summary.title: Stream-R1: Reliability-Perplexity Aware Reward Distillation for Streaming Video Generation

details: Distribution matching distillation (DMD) for autoregressive streaming video generation weights every rollout, frame, and pixel equally, even though the DMD gradient varies in how reliably it points toward the teacher's high-quality mode (Inter-Reliability) and different spatiotemporal regions differ in remaining improvement potential (Intra-Perplexity).

Stream-R1: a reward-guided reweighting of the DMD loss with two levels derived from a single pretrained video reward model — a per-rollout scalar multiplier exp(beta * reward) and a per-element spatiotemporal weight map obtained by back-propagating the reward score to the input pixels to get gradient saliency.

The saliency volume is factorized into separately normalized temporal (per-frame) and spatial (per-frame-normalized) weights, multiplied and mean-normalized, so loss magnitude is preserved while optimization concentrates on reward-sensitive regions/frames.

Multi-dimensional balancing: per-axis saliencies (visual quality, motion quality, text alignment) are fused with softmax weights favoring the currently weakest axis, plus a reward penalty on the standard deviation of per-axis improvement trajectories.
Built on the Reward Forcing framework; student = Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B, teacher = Wan2.1-T2V-14B, 4-step distilled causal student generating 5s videos at 832x480
Initialized from an ODE-regression checkpoint (16k ODE pairs, following CausVid); chunk-wise denoising with 3 latent frames per chunk, denoising steps [1000,750,500,250], attention window 9
Training prompts from filtered VidProM with LLM prompt rewriting
Saliency combination temperature tau = 1.0; spatial weight floor sigma_min = 0.15; temporal floor tau_min = 0.20; reward inverse temperature beta = 2.0 on the Overall (mean of VQ/MQ/TA) reward

1,000 optimizer steps on 8 A100 GPUs, effective batch size 64, AdamW with lr 2e-6 (generator) and 4e-7 (fake score), generator updated every 5 steps, EMA 0.99 from step 200, ~56 GPU-hours-scale run (approx. 56 hours total)
Short video: 946 VBench prompts (rewritten with Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct), 5 seeds; Total/Quality/Semantic scores plus FPS
Long video: 10s/30s/60s/120s/180s from first 128 MovieGen Video Bench prompts with block-wise autoregressive generation and EMA-Sink attention; six VBench metrics plus a drift measure
VLM judging with Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B (1-5 on visual, dynamic, text) on 60s videos; human A/B preference study on 50 60s videos, 5 annotators, five dimensions
Controlled diagnostic: Gaussian blur injected into the lower half of frames with the corrupted area expanding across frames, then inspecting reward-gradient saliency and temporal weights

Baselines: diffusion (LTX-Video, Wan2.1), autoregressive/streaming (SkyReels-V2, MAGI-1, NOVA, Pyramid Flow, CausVid, Self Forcing, LongLive, Rolling Forcing), and reward-guided distillation (Reward Forcing, the direct baseline)

Ablations progressively add spatial saliency, balanced multi-dimensional reward, and temporal decomposition on a no-reward DMD baseline; sensitivity sweeps of sigma_min (0.15 vs 0.30) and tau_min (0.20 vs 0.40)

key_findings.finding: Decomposing a scalar video reward into spatiotemporally localized DMD weights improves all VBench axes over the global-scalar reward baseline at zero inference cost.
key_findings.evidence: Stream-R1 vs Reward Forcing on 946 VBench prompts: Total 84.40 vs 84.13, Quality 85.14 vs 84.84, Semantic 81.44 vs 81.32 (+0.27/+0.30/+0.12), identical 23.1 FPS; Quality closes over 60% of the gap to the multi-step teacher Wan2.1 (85.30).

key_findings.finding: The 4-step distilled student surpasses its own multi-step bidirectional teacher on overall and semantic quality.
key_findings.evidence: Stream-R1 Total 84.40 vs Wan2.1 84.26 and Semantic 81.44 vs 80.09, at roughly 30x higher inference speed (23.1 vs 0.78 FPS).

key_findings.finding: Temporal saliency weighting is the single most important component, and it also reduces long-horizon quality drift.
key_findings.evidence: Ablation: adding temporal reward raises Short Total from 83.68 to 84.40 (+0.72) and lowers Drift from 2.697 to 2.417 (baseline drift 2.479); raising the temporal floor to tau_min=0.40 collapses Short Total to 83.42, below the spatial-only variant.

key_findings.finding: Benefits grow with video length, indicating slower quality collapse in long autoregressive rollouts.
key_findings.evidence: Across 10s to 180s on 128 MovieGen prompts, Stream-R1 beats Reward Forcing on all six VBench metrics at every duration, with the gap widening most at 120s and 180s where Reward Forcing degrades more steeply.

key_findings.finding: Reward-model gradient saliency emergently localizes actual quality deficiency in both space and time.
key_findings.evidence: In the controlled blur experiment, saliency concentrates on the blurred lower half rather than the intact upper half and migrates into the expanding corrupted region, while per-frame temporal weights grow monotonically from 0.587 to 2.117 as the degraded area enlarges.
